'''Anna Fontcuberta i Morral''' is the president of [[École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne|École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)]] in [[Switzerland]], succeeding [[Martin Vetterli]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Presidency |url=https://www.epfl.ch/about/presidency/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=EPFL |language=en-GB}}</ref> She is a Spanish and Swiss physicist and [[Materials science|materials scientist]]. Her research focuses on [[nanotechnology]] applied in the production of [[solar cell]]s and quantum technologies. She is a full professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] (EPFL) and the head of the Laboratory of Semiconductor Materials.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LMSC|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lmsc/|access-date=2020-09-28|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=25 new professors appointed at the two Federal Institutes of Technology {{!}} ETH-Board|url=https://www.ethrat.ch/en/media/releases/appointments-september19|access-date=2020-09-28|website=www.ethrat.ch|archive-date=2020-11-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122095524/https://www.ethrat.ch/en/media/releases/appointments-september19}}</ref><ref name="president_release" />

== Career ==
Fontcuberta i Morral studied physics at [[University of Barcelona]] and received her Bachelor's degree in 1997. In the following year she gained a diploma (Diplôme d'Etudes Approfondis, D.E.A.) in [[materials science]] from [[Université Paris-Sud]]. As a graduate student she joined the group of Pere Roca i Cabarrocas at [[École Polytechnique|Ecole Polytechnique]] in [[Palaiseau]], France, and graduated in 2001 with a PhD in materials science.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fontcuberta i Morral|first1=A|last2=Roca i Cabarrocas|first2=P|date=20 February 2001|title=Shedding light on the growth of amorphous, polymorphous, protocrystalline and microcrystalline silicon thin films|journal=Thin Solid Films|volume=383|issue=1–2|pages=161–164|doi=10.1016/s0040-6090(00)01596-0|bibcode=2001TSF...383..161F|issn=0040-6090}}</ref> She then went to the [[California Institute of Technology]] to work as postdoctoral scholar with [[Harry Atwater|Harry A. Atwater]].<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Zahler|first1=J.M.|last2=Fontcuberta i Morral|first2=A.|last3=Chang-Geun Ahn|last4=Atwater|first4=H.A.|last5=Wanlass|first5=M.W.|last6=Chu|first6=C.|last7=Iles|first7=P.A.|title=Conference Record of the Twenty-Ninth IEEE Photovoltaic Specialists Conference, 2002 |chapter=Wafer bonding and layer transfer processes for 4-junction high efficiency solar cells |date=2002|chapter-url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/1190783|location=New Orleans, LA, USA|publisher=IEEE|pages=1039–1042|doi=10.1109/PVSC.2002.1190783|osti=15006757|isbn=978-0-7803-7471-3|s2cid=18500749|url=https://authors.library.caltech.edu/12629/ }}</ref>

In 2003, she became a permanent research fellow at [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] at the [[École Polytechnique]]. From 2004 to 2005 she was visiting scientist at [[California Institute of Technology]]. During this time she co-founded the startup company Aonex Technologies specialized in layer transfer for the production of multi-junction solar cells.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=EPS Emmy Noether Distinction Spring 2015 for Women in Physics {{!}} e-EPS|url=http://www.epsnews.eu/2015/07/eps-emmy-noether-distinction-spring-2015-for-women-in-physics/|access-date=2020-09-28|website=www.epsnews.eu}}</ref> Sponsored by a Marie Curie Excellence Grant she became team leader at the Walter Schottky Institute at the [[Technical University of Munich]] in 2005, where she also habilitated in physics in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|title=TUM Ambassador Anna Fontcuberta i Morral|url=https://www.together.tum.de/aktuelles/veroeffentlichungen/2014/09/02/anna-fontcuberta-i-morral/|access-date=2020-09-28|language=en-US}}{{Dead link|date=August 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hetzl|first1=Martin|last2=Kraut|first2=Max|last3=Winnerl|first3=Julia|last4=Francaviglia|first4=Luca|last5=Döblinger|first5=Markus|last6=Matich|first6=Sonja|last7=Fontcuberta i Morral|first7=Anna|last8=Stutzmann|first8=Martin|date=9 November 2016|title=Strain-Induced Band Gap Engineering in Selectively Grown GaN–(Al,Ga)N Core–Shell Nanowire Heterostructures|journal=Nano Letters|volume=16|issue=11|pages=7098–7106|doi=10.1021/acs.nanolett.6b03354|pmid=27766884|bibcode=2016NanoL..16.7098H|issn=1530-6984 |url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/225111 }}</ref> There, she started her independent research activities on III-V-based [[nanowire]]s.

In 2008, she joined the Institute of Materials Science & Engineering at the School of Engineering of [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] as an assistant professor. In 2014 and 2019, she was successively promoted to associate and full professor.<ref>{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=25 new professors appointed at the two Federal Institutes of Technology |url=https://ethrat.ch/en/25-new-professors-appointed-at-the-two-federal-institutes-of-technology/ |location= |publisher= |agency=ETH Board |date=26 September 2019 |access-date=2024-03-27}}</ref><ref name="president_release" /> She is the founder and head of the Laboratory of Semiconductor Materials.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=People|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lmsc/page-123565-en-html/|access-date=2020-09-28|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> Since January 2021, she is the associate vice-president for Centers and Platforms at EPFL.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Vice Presidency for Academic Affairs (VPA)|url=https://www.epfl.ch/about/vice-presidencies/vice-presidency-for-academic-affairs-vpa/|access-date=2021-03-11|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> She also served as the president of the EPFL WISH foundation between 2018 and 2020, a foundation whose goal is to support EPFL female students to excel in their careers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Current Team|url=https://www.epflwishfoundation.org/members|access-date=2021-03-11|website=wishfoundation-2|language=en}}</ref>

Starting 1 January 2025, the [[Federal Council (Switzerland)|Swiss Federal Council]] appointed her as the sixth President of EPFL for a 4-year term, succeeding [[Martin Vetterli]]. She is the first woman to hold the position.<ref name="president_release">{{cite press release |author=<!--Not stated--> |title=Anna Fontcuberta i Morral named as new EPFL president |url=https://www.admin.ch/gov/en/start/documentation/media-releases/media-releases-federal-council.msg-id-100549.html |location=Bern, Switzerland |publisher= |agency=Federal Council |date=27 March 2024 |access-date=2024-03-27}}</ref>

Fontcuberta i Morral is a member of the Executive Advisory Board of the [[World.minds|World.Minds]] Foundation, participating in global discussions on science, technology, and education.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Team – WORLD.MINDS |url=https://www.worldminds.org/team/ |access-date=2025-05-15 |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==

sustainable material design.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lmsc/page-79450-en-html/|access-date=2020-09-28|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite == Distinctions ==
In 2012, she received EPFL's Rodolphe and Renée Haenny Fondation Prize.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Vandevyver|first=Caroline|date=10 October 2012|title=Rodolphe and Renée Haenny Prize 2012 – A. i Morral and H. Frauenrath|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/rodolphe-and-renee-haenny-prize-2012-a-i-morral-an/|language=en}}</ref> In 2015, she was awarded the [[European Physical Society]]'s [[Emmy Noether]] Distinction for "noteworthy women physicists".<ref name=":1" />

She has received prestigious research grants from the [[European Research Council]] and the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ERC FUNDED PROJECTS|url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results|access-date=2021-03-05|website=ERC: European Research Council|language=en|archive-date=2021-01-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210113223931/https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results}}</ref>
